co_west_fork.blurb: A small roadside bouldering spot in the West Fork drainage, at the western foot of Wolf Creek Pass near Pagosa Springs. It holds eleven problems, most of them between VB and V3, with a handful of harder lines up to V5. Some problems sit right beside the road and a few more are on a separate block near the river. It sees very little traffic, so holds stay unchalked, and there is more rock further up in the trees for anyone willing to wander. Bring a pad; the problems run up to about fifteen feet. It is better as a stop while passing through than as a trip in its own right.

co_b_genesis_wall.blurb: The Genesis Wall is the second cluster of bolted lines met on the way down into Cascade Canyon north of Durango, just beyond the smaller wall at the canyon entrance. Eleven sport routes here are mostly 5.11 and 5.12, with a single 5.9 to ease in. The limestone is vertical and technical, and the pitches are short, roughly 35 to 45 feet. A few trees give some shade and a level spot to sit, which makes the base a handy place to start or finish a day.

co_g_restaurant_row.blurb: Restaurant Row is a small crag on the far side of the creek from the rest of Cascade Canyon's climbing, north of Durango. Ten sport routes and one trad line cover a wide spread, from easy 5.7 and 5.9 up through a cluster of 5.10s and on to several at 5.11 and 5.12. It is often passed over, though the rock is good. The face catches the sun early and falls into shade through the afternoon, which suits summer days. Reaching it means crossing the creek, which can be awkward in early summer and is usually easy later in the season.

co_guano_boulder.blurb: A chalky boulder tucked away in the Bone Park boulders of Unaweep Canyon, near Grand Junction. Eleven problems cover its faces, nearly all between V1 and V3: six at V2, four at V3 and one V1, so it suits a session of moderate climbing rather than hard projects. The landing is good, and a couple of pads are plenty. Reaching it means a short trail walk from the parking at Bone Park, down to the creek, across it and back up the hill on the far side until the slope flattens and the boulder appears.

co_long_hill.blurb: Long Hill is a small granite crag in the South Platte country, close to the entrance of the Goose Creek area but just outside it, reached along the Forest Road 211 route from Pine. It holds eleven routes, mostly traditional, with a few bolted lines and one boulder problem. Most of the climbing sits around 5.10, with a few easier lines below. The cliff is split into two separate sections, one with only a few routes and the other with the bulk of them; its main face has room for new crack lines. Expect a quiet day on rock with the knobby, friction-rich texture typical of the district.

co_pinnacle_colada.blurb: Pinnacle Colada is a tall, thumb-shaped block on Flagstaff Mountain above Boulder, the first prominent pinnacle uphill and north of the First Overhang boulder. Its eleven problems range from VB-level warm-ups to a couple of hard lines at V6 and V7, with the bulk in the V3 to V4 middle. Many are highballs, so pads and a spotter matter. The south face has a slab that makes a good easy line and the best way back down, while the corners and arete offer pocketed and crack climbing on thinner holds.
